import OAI.Algorithms.SubexponentialSAT.LeanCompat
import OAI.Algorithms.SubexponentialSAT.WeightedSupport
import OAI.Algorithms.SubexponentialSAT.NilpotentDefect

namespace OAI.Algorithms

/-!
# Canonical truncation before substitution

Polynomials are represented with U outermost, Z in the middle, and the X variables
innermost.  Truncation is an operation on canonical polynomial representatives;
we never assert that U = 1 defines a map out of the truncated quotient.
-/

namespace SubexponentialSAT.Truncation

noncomputable section

open scoped BigOperators

variable {R ι : Type*} [CommSemiring R]

abbrev Poly (ι R : Type*) [CommSemiring R] :=
  Polynomial (Polynomial (MvPolynomial ι R))

/-- Delete all coefficients of degree at least n. -/
def trunc {A : Type*} [Semiring A] (n : ℕ) (P : Polynomial A) : Polynomial A :=
  Polynomial.ofFinsupp (.ofCoeff (P.toFinsupp.coeff.filter fun j => j < n))

@[simp] theorem coeff_trunc {A : Type*} [Semiring A]
    (n j : ℕ) (P : Polynomial A) :
    (trunc n P).coeff j = if j < n then P.coeff j else 0 := by
  classical
  simp [trunc, Polynomial.coeff, Finsupp.filter_apply]

@[simp] theorem trunc_zero {A : Type*} [Semiring A] (n : ℕ) :
    trunc n (0 : Polynomial A) = 0 := by
  ext j
  simp

@[simp] theorem trunc_add {A : Type*} [Semiring A]
    (n : ℕ) (P Q : Polynomial A) :
    trunc n (P + Q) = trunc n P + trunc n Q := by
  ext j
  by_cases h : j < n <;> simp [h]

/-- Delete X monomials whose total degree exceeds N. -/
def xTrunc (N : ℕ) (P : MvPolynomial ι R) : MvPolynomial ι R :=
  .ofCoeff ((AddMonoidAlgebra.coeff P).filter
    fun a : ι →₀ ℕ => a.sum (fun _ k => k) ≤ N)

@[simp] theorem coeff_xTrunc (N : ℕ) (a : ι →₀ ℕ) (P : MvPolynomial ι R) :
    (xTrunc N P).coeff a =
      if a.sum (fun _ k => k) ≤ N then P.coeff a else 0 := by
  classical
  simp [xTrunc, Finsupp.filter_apply]

@[simp] theorem xTrunc_zero (N : ℕ) : xTrunc N (0 : MvPolynomial ι R) = 0 := by
  ext a
  simp

import OAI.Algorithms.SubexponentialSAT.LeanCompat
import OAI.Algorithms.SubexponentialSAT.Incidence
import OAI.Algorithms.SubexponentialSAT.Types

namespace OAI.Algorithms

/-!
# Incidence slots and globally consistent factor words

Section 5.4 assigns each coordinate's incident factors to different slots.
The same factor word is then used at every incidence of that factor.  The
slot numbers themselves need not agree at different coordinates.

The ordered constructor and the slot-filling operations are computable.  An
additional constructor for arbitrary finite factor types chooses an enumeration.
No running-time bound or probabilistic independence assertion is hidden here.
-/

namespace SubexponentialSAT.SlotAssignment

open SubexponentialSAT.Factor SubexponentialSAT.Types

variable {V E : Type*} [DecidableEq V]

/-- The actual factors incident to one coordinate. -/
abbrev Incident (P : Pattern V E) (v : V) := {e : E // v ∈ P.scope e}

/-- An injective slot assignment separately at each coordinate. -/
abbrev SlotMap (P : Pattern V E) (Δ : ℕ) :=
  (v : V) → Incident P v ↪ Fin Δ

@[simp] theorem card_incident [Fintype E] (P : Pattern V E) (v : V) :
    Fintype.card (Incident P v) =
      (Finset.univ.filter fun e => v ∈ P.scope e).card := by
  exact Fintype.card_subtype _

/-- The incidence bound supplies exactly the cardinal inequality needed for slots. -/
theorem card_incident_le [Fintype E] (P : Pattern V E) {k Δ : ℕ}
    (hP : P.Bounded k Δ) (v : V) : Fintype.card (Incident P v) ≤ Δ := by
  rw [card_incident]
  exact hP.incidence_le v

/-- A finite slot assignment, using a chosen enumeration for each incident set. -/
noncomputable def slotsOfCardLE [Fintype E] (P : Pattern V E) {Δ : ℕ}
    (h : ∀ v, Fintype.card (Incident P v) ≤ Δ) : SlotMap P Δ :=
  fun v => (Fintype.equivFin (Incident P v)).toEmbedding.trans (Fin.castLEEmb (h v))

/-- Slot assignments exist for every bounded factor pattern. -/
noncomputable def slotsOfBounded [Fintype E] (P : Pattern V E) {k Δ : ℕ}
    (hP : P.Bounded k Δ) : SlotMap P Δ :=
  slotsOfCardLE P (card_incident_le P hP)

/-- For ordered factor indices, sort the incident factors and use their ranks.
This constructor makes the fixed local ordering in the exposition explicit. -/
def orderedSlotsOfCardLE [Fintype E] [LinearOrder E] (P : Pattern V E) {Δ : ℕ}
    (h : ∀ v, Fintype.card (Incident P v) ≤ Δ) : SlotMap P Δ :=
  fun v => (Fintype.orderIsoFinOfCardEq (Incident P v) rfl).symm.toEquiv.toEmbedding.trans
    (Fin.castLEEmb (h v))

/-- Computable slot assignment for a bounded pattern with ordered factor indices. -/

/-!
# Incidence slots and globally consistent factor words

Section 5.4 assigns each coordinate's incident factors to different slots.
The same factor word is then used at every incidence of that factor.  The
slot numbers themselves need not agree at different coordinates.

The ordered constructor and the slot-filling operations are computable.  An
additional constructor for arbitrary finite factor types chooses an enumeration.
No running-time bound or probabilistic independence assertion is hidden here.
-/

namespace SubexponentialSAT.SlotAssignment

open SubexponentialSAT.Factor SubexponentialSAT.Types

variable {V E : Type*} [DecidableEq V]

/-- The actual factors incident to one coordinate. -/
abbrev Incident (P : Pattern V E) (v : V) := {e : E // v ∈ P.scope e}

/-- An injective slot assignment separately at each coordinate. -/
abbrev SlotMap (P : Pattern V E) (Δ : ℕ) :=
  (v : V) → Incident P v ↪ Fin Δ

@[simp] theorem card_incident [Fintype E] (P : Pattern V E) (v : V) :
    Fintype.card (Incident P v) =
      (Finset.univ.filter fun e => v ∈ P.scope e).card := by
  exact Fintype.card_subtype _

/-- The incidence bound supplies exactly the cardinal inequality needed for slots. -/
theorem card_incident_le [Fintype E] (P : Pattern V E) {k Δ : ℕ}
    (hP : P.Bounded k Δ) (v : V) : Fintype.card (Incident P v) ≤ Δ := by
  rw [card_incident]
  exact hP.incidence_le v

/-- A finite slot assignment, using a chosen enumeration for each incident set. -/
noncomputable def slotsOfCardLE [Fintype E] (P : Pattern V E) {Δ : ℕ}
    (h : ∀ v, Fintype.card (Incident P v) ≤ Δ) : SlotMap P Δ :=
  fun v => (Fintype.equivFin (Incident P v)).toEmbedding.trans (Fin.castLEEmb (h v))

/-- Slot assignments exist for every bounded factor pattern. -/
noncomputable def slotsOfBounded [Fintype E] (P : Pattern V E) {k Δ : ℕ}
    (hP : P.Bounded k Δ) : SlotMap P Δ :=
  slotsOfCardLE P (card_incident_le P hP)

/-- For ordered factor indices, sort the incident factors and use their ranks.
This constructor makes the fixed local ordering in the exposition explicit. -/
def orderedSlotsOfCardLE [Fintype E] [LinearOrder E] (P : Pattern V E) {Δ : ℕ}
    (h : ∀ v, Fintype.card (Incident P v) ≤ Δ) : SlotMap P Δ :=
  fun v => (Fintype.orderIsoFinOfCardEq (Incident P v) rfl).symm.toEquiv.toEmbedding.trans
    (Fin.castLEEmb (h v))

/-!
# MODULE: q2_expert_blob_geometry
SOURCES: include/strata/kernels/cpu/expert.hpp, src/kernels/cpu/expert.cpp, src/kernels/cpu/expert_layout.cpp
Fixes the geometry of one Q2_0 routed expert (H=2560, FF=640, QK=64, QKA=32) and the byte layout of its
1,382,400-byte blob, and proves every row/scale address the kernels form stays inside its region.  Also
models the CPUID feature gate (`CpuFeatures::usable`, `cpu_avx512_ok`).

## Source semantics
* A Q2_0 weight block is QK=64 two-bit codes (16 bytes) plus one fp16 scale (2 bytes) = BB=18 bytes.
* An activation chunk is QKA=32 int8 values with its own scale, so ONE weight block spans TWO chunks.
* Blob layout: gate/up codes [2*FF rows x 640 B] | down codes [H rows x 160 B] |
  gate/up scales [2*FF x 40 fp16] | down scales [H x 10 fp16]; the four regions tile the blob exactly.
* Gate row r is interleaved row 2r, up row r is row 2r+1.
* The expert kernel is usable iff AVX512F, BW, VL, VNNI and VBMI are all present (CPUID leaf 7:
  EBX bits 16,30,31; ECX bits 11,1); `cpu_avx512_ok` additionally requires OSXSAVE and XCR0 & 0xE6 = 0xE6.

## Form template identifiers
H → embedWidth, FF → ffWidth, QK → weightBlock, QKA → actChunk, BB → blockBytes, BLOB → blobBytes,
O_GU_CODES/O_D_CODES/O_GU_SCALES/O_D_SCALES → regionOffset_{guCodes,dCodes,guScales,dScales},
CpuFeatures.usable → featureGate, cpu_avx512_ok → osFeatureGate
-/

namespace Strata.Kernels.Cpu.Geometry

-- § constants (expert.hpp)

def H : Nat := 2560
def FF : Nat := 640
def NE : Nat := 512
def QK : Nat := 64
def QKA : Nat := 32
def BB : Nat := 18
def MAXC : Nat := H / QKA
def ROW_GU : Nat := H * 2 / 8
def ROW_D : Nat := FF * 2 / 8
def SC_GU : Nat := H / QK
def SC_D : Nat := FF / QK
def BLOB : Nat := 3 * (H * FF * BB / QK)

def O_GU_CODES : Nat := 0
def O_D_CODES : Nat := 2 * FF * ROW_GU
def O_GU_SCALES : Nat := O_D_CODES + H * ROW_D
def O_D_SCALES : Nat := O_GU_SCALES + 2 * FF * SC_GU * 2

-- § evaluated constants

/-- 80 activation chunks across the widest reduction. -/
theorem maxc_val : MAXC = 80 := by decide

/-- 640 code bytes per gate/up row. -/
theorem row_gu_val : ROW_GU = 640 := by decide

/-- 160 code bytes per down row. -/
theorem row_d_val : ROW_D = 160 := by decide

/-- 40 weight blocks per gate/up row. -/
theorem sc_gu_val : SC_GU = 40 := by decide

/-- 10 weight blocks per down row. -/
theorem sc_d_val : SC_D = 10 := by decide

/-- The header's stated blob size. -/
theorem blob_val : BLOB = 1382400 := by decide

/-- Region offsets, evaluated. -/
theorem offsets_val :
    O_D_CODES = 819200 ∧ O_GU_SCALES = 1228800 ∧ O_D_SCALES = 1331200 := by decide

-- § block contract

/-- THE contract: a 64-weight block covers exactly two 32-element activation chunks. -/
theorem weight_block_spans_two_chunks : QK = 2 * QKA := by decide

/-- 18 bytes per block = 16 code bytes (2 bits per weight) + one fp16 scale. -/
theorem block_bytes : QK * 2 / 8 + 2 = BB := by decide

/-- A row's code bytes are 16 per weight block. -/
theorem row_codes_per_block : ROW_GU = SC_GU * 16 ∧ ROW_D = SC_D * 16 := by decide

/-- The four regions tile the blob exactly: the last region ends at `BLOB`. -/
theorem layout_tiles_blob : O_D_SCALES + H * SC_D * 2 = BLOB := by decide

/-- The blob equals three matrices of H*FF Q2_0 weights at 18 bytes per 64. -/
theorem blob_three_matrices : BLOB = (2 * FF * H + H * FF) * BB / QK := by decide

-- § addresses stay in their regions

/-- Gate row 2r and up row 2r+1 codes lie inside the gate/up code region. -/
theorem gu_codes_in_region (r : Nat) (hr : r < FF) :
    O_GU_CODES + (2 * r + 1) * ROW_GU + ROW_GU ≤ O_D_CODES := by
  have h1 : ROW_GU = 640 := row_gu_val
  have h2 : O_D_CODES = 819200 := offsets_val.1
  have h3 : FF = 640 := rfl
  rw [h1, h2]
  simp only [O_GU_CODES]
  omega

/-- Down row r's codes lie inside the down code region. -/
theorem d_codes_in_region (r : Nat) (hr : r < H) :
    O_D_CODES + r * ROW_D + ROW_D ≤ O_GU_SCALES := by
  have h1 : ROW_D = 160 := row_d_val
  have h2 := offsets_val
  have h3 : H = 2560 := rfl
  rw [h1, h2.1, h2.2.1]
  omega

/-- Gate/up scale rows lie inside the gate/up scale region. -/
theorem gu_scales_in_region (r : Nat) (hr : r < FF) :
    O_GU_SCALES + (2 * r + 1) * SC_GU * 2 + SC_GU * 2 ≤ O_D_SCALES := by
  have h1 : SC_GU = 40 := sc_gu_val
  have h2 := offsets_val
  have h3 : FF = 640 := rfl
  rw [h1, h2.2.1, h2.2.2]
  omega

/-- Down scale rows lie inside the last region, hence inside the blob. -/
theorem d_scales_in_blob (r : Nat) (hr : r < H) :
    O_D_SCALES + r * SC_D * 2 + SC_D * 2 ≤ BLOB := by
  have h1 : SC_D = 10 := sc_d_val
  have h2 := offsets_val
  have h3 : H = 2560 := rfl
  have h4 : BLOB = 1382400 := blob_val
  rw [h1, h2.2.2, h4]
  omega

/-- Weight j of block b in a gate/up row reads code byte `b*16 + j/4`, which is inside the row. -/
theorem code_byte_in_row (b j : Nat) (hb : b < SC_GU) (hj : j < QK) :
    b * 16 + j / 4 < ROW_GU := by
  have h1 : SC_GU = 40 := sc_gu_val
  have h2 : ROW_GU = 640 := row_gu_val
  have h3 : QK = 64 := rfl
  rw [h1] at hb; rw [h3] at hj; rw [h2]
  omega

/-- Block b uses activation chunks 2b and 2b+1, both inside the 80-chunk scale arrays. -/
theorem block_chunks_in_range (b : Nat) (hb : b < SC_GU) : 2 * b + 1 < MAXC := by
  have h1 : SC_GU = 40 := sc_gu_val
  have h2 : MAXC = 80 := maxc_val
  rw [h1] at hb; rw [h2]
  omega

/-- The chunk of element i is `i / QKA`, and for i in the block it is one of the block's two chunks. -/
theorem element_chunk_of_block (b j : Nat) (hj : j < QK) :
    (b * QK + j) / QKA = 2 * b ∨ (b * QK + j) / QKA = 2 * b + 1 := by
  have h3 : QK = 64 := rfl
  have h4 : QKA = 32 := rfl
  rw [h3] at hj ⊢; rw [h4]
  omega

-- § CPU feature gate

/-- The five feature flags the kernel needs. -/
structure CpuFeatures where
  avx512f : Bool
  avx512bw : Bool
  avx512vl : Bool
  avx512_vnni : Bool
  avx512_vbmi : Bool

/-- `CpuFeatures::usable`. -/
def CpuFeatures.usable (f : CpuFeatures) : Bool :=
  f.avx512f && f.avx512bw && f.avx512vl && f.avx512_vnni && f.avx512_vbmi

/-- The CPUID leaf-7 bit extraction of `cpu_features()`. -/
def featuresOf (ebx ecx : Nat) : CpuFeatures :=
  { avx512f := ebx.testBit 16, avx512bw := ebx.testBit 30, avx512vl := ebx.testBit 31,
    avx512_vnni := ecx.testBit 11, avx512_vbmi := ecx.testBit 1 }

/-- Usable exactly when every one of the five flags is set (missing ANY one refuses). -/
theorem usable_iff (f : CpuFeatures) :
    f.usable = true ↔ f.avx512f = true ∧ f.avx512bw = true ∧ f.avx512vl = true ∧
      f.avx512_vnni = true ∧ f.avx512_vbmi = true := by
  cases f with
  | mk a b c d e => cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> cases d <;> cases e <;> decide

/-- A machine with AVX-512F/BW/VL but no VNNI is refused. -/
theorem refused_without_vnni (f : CpuFeatures) (h : f.avx512_vnni = false) : f.usable = false := by
  cases f with
  | mk a b c d e =>
    simp only [CpuFeatures.usable] at h ⊢
    rw [h]
    cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> rfl

/-- `cpu_avx512_ok`: OSXSAVE, the OS-saved XCR0 state mask, and the same five CPUID bits. -/
def osFeatureGate (ecx1 xcr0 ebx7 ecx7 : Nat) : Bool :=
  ecx1.testBit 27 && (xcr0 &&& 0xE6 == 0xE6) && (featuresOf ebx7 ecx7).usable

/-- The XCR0 mask 0xE6 is SSE, AVX, opmask, ZMM_Hi256 and Hi16_ZMM state (bits 1,2,5,6,7). -/
theorem xcr0_mask_bits : (0xE6 : Nat) = 2 ^ 1 + 2 ^ 2 + 2 ^ 5 + 2 ^ 6 + 2 ^ 7 := by decide

/-- The OS gate implies the CPU-only gate: it can only refuse more machines, never fewer. -/
theorem osGate_implies_usable (e1 x b c : Nat) (h : osFeatureGate e1 x b c = true) :
    (featuresOf b c).usable = true := by
  simp only [osFeatureGate, Bool.and_eq_true] at h
  exact h.2

/-- Example: a fully featured EBX/ECX pair is usable. -/
theorem full_features_usable :
    (featuresOf (2 ^ 16 + 2 ^ 30 + 2 ^ 31) (2 ^ 11 + 2 ^ 1)).usable = true := by decide

end Strata.Kernels.Cpu.Geometry

SOURCES: src/kernels/cpu/expert.cpp, src/kernels/cpu/q2_avx2.cpp, include/strata/kernels/cpu/expert.hpp

`row_dot_multi`, `q2g_row_multi`, the AVX2 `row_multi`): 2-bit code unpacking, the offset identity
`Σ (c-1)·x = Σ c·x − Σ x`, the two-chunks-per-block scale contract with the precomputed `hx`
correction, and the per-token equivalence of the multi-token kernels.  Exact integer arithmetic stands
in for real arithmetic; FP32 evaluation order is the only thing the kernels change.

## Source semantics
* Code of weight i in a 16-byte block: byte i/4, bits 2·(i%4), masked with 3, so it lies in {0,1,2,3};
  the dequantized weight is (code − 1)·d ∈ {−d, 0, d, 2d}.
* Per chunk, `Σ (c−1)·d_w·x̂·d_x = d_w·(d_x·Σ c·x̂ − d_x·Σ x̂)`; the second term is `hx = d_x·sum`,
  weight-independent, precomputed once per layer.
* A 64-weight block uses TWO activation scales (chunks 2b, 2b+1); one scale per block is a real error.
* `chunk_dot_oracle` subtracts the integer sum before conversion; the result is the same exact value.
* Multi-token kernels unpack codes once and give each token exactly the single-token value.

## Form template identifiers
code → unpackCode, offDot → exactOffsetDot, cDot → codeDot, xSum → actSum, hx → chunkCorrection,
Chunk/Block → actChunk/weightBlock, exactRow → referenceRowDot, kernelAcc/kernelCorr → vnniAccumulator/
correctionAccumulator, oracleRow → oracleRowDot, rowMulti → multiTokenRowDot

/-- Code k (0..3) of a byte: `(byte >> 2k) & 3`. -/
def code (byte k : Nat) : Nat := (byte >>> (2 * k)) % 4

/-- Every code is a 2-bit value. -/
theorem code_lt_four (byte k : Nat) : code byte k < 4 := Nat.mod_lt _ (by decide)

/-- Pack four 2-bit codes into a byte, low code first (the GGUF/Strata order). -/
def pack4 (c0 c1 c2 c3 : Nat) : Nat := c0 + 4 * c1 + 16 * c2 + 64 * c3

/-- Unpacking inverts packing: code k of `pack4` is the k-th code. -/
theorem code_pack4 (c0 c1 c2 c3 : Nat) (h0 : c0 < 4) (h1 : c1 < 4) (h2 : c2 < 4) (h3 : c3 < 4) :
    code (pack4 c0 c1 c2 c3) 0 = c0 ∧ code (pack4 c0 c1 c2 c3) 1 = c1 ∧
      code (pack4 c0 c1 c2 c3) 2 = c2 ∧ code (pack4 c0 c1 c2 c3) 3 = c3 := by
  simp only [code, pack4, Nat.shiftRight_eq_div_pow]
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> simp <;> omega

/-- A packed byte is a byte. -/
theorem pack4_lt (c0 c1 c2 c3 : Nat) (h0 : c0 < 4) (h1 : c1 < 4) (h2 : c2 < 4) (h3 : c3 < 4) :
    pack4 c0 c1 c2 c3 < 256 := by
  simp only [pack4]; omega

/-- Weight i (< 64) of a block is in byte i/4 (< 16) at code position i%4 (< 4). -/
theorem unpack_position (i : Nat) (hi : i < 64) : i / 4 < 16 ∧ i % 4 < 4 ∧ 4 * (i / 4) + i % 4 = i := by
  omega

/-- The dequantized code offset `code − 1` lies in {−1,0,1,2}. -/
theorem code_offset_range (byte k : Nat) :
    -1 ≤ (code byte k : Int) - 1 ∧ (code byte k : Int) - 1 ≤ 2 := by
  have h := code_lt_four byte k
  omega

/-- Exact reference: `Σ (c−1)·x` over (code, activation) pairs. -/

  | [] => 0
  | (c, x) :: t => (c - 1) * x + offDot t

/-- The VNNI integer dot `Σ c·x`. -/
def cDot : List (Int × Int) → Int
  | [] => 0
  | (c, x) :: t => c * x + cDot t

/-- The activation sum `Σ x` (the chunk's `sum`). -/
def xSum : List (Int × Int) → Int
  | [] => 0
  | (_, x) :: t => x + xSum t

/-- The Q2_0 identity: the −1 code offset is a weight-independent correction. -/
theorem offDot_eq (l : List (Int × Int)) : offDot l = cDot l - xSum l := by
  induction l with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons p t ih =>
    obtain ⟨c, x⟩ := p
    simp only [offDot, cDot, xSum]
    rw [ih, Int.sub_mul, Int.one_mul]
    generalize c * x = cx
    omega

/-- One 32-element activation chunk with its own scale `s` (exact, as an integer stand-in). -/

  pairs : List (Int × Int)

def hx (ch : Chunk) : Int := ch.s * xSum ch.pairs

def exactChunk (ch : Chunk) : Int := ch.s * offDot ch.pairs

theorem exactChunk_eq (ch : Chunk) : exactChunk ch = ch.s * cDot ch.pairs - hx ch := by
  unfold exactChunk hx
  rw [offDot_eq, Int.mul_sub]

/-- One 64-weight block: one weight scale `d`, two chunks with two scales. -/
structure Block where
  d : Int
  lo : Chunk
  hi : Chunk

/-- Reference block value `d · (lo + hi)` with each chunk on its own scale. -/
def exactBlock (b : Block) : Int := b.d * (exactChunk b.lo + exactChunk b.hi)

/-- Reference row: the sum over blocks. -/
def exactRow : List Block → Int
  | [] => 0
  | b :: t => exactBlock b + exactRow t

/-- The kernel's float accumulator: `Σ d·s_lo·cDot_lo + d·s_hi·cDot_hi`. -/
def kernelAcc : List Block → Int
  | [] => 0
  | b :: t => b.d * b.lo.s * cDot b.lo.pairs + b.d * b.hi.s * cDot b.hi.pairs + kernelAcc t

/-- The kernel's correction accumulator: `Σ d·(hx_lo + hx_hi)`. -/
def kernelCorr : List Block → Int
  | [] => 0
  | b :: t => b.d * (hx b.lo + hx b.hi) + kernelCorr t

/-- One block of the kernel equals the reference block. -/
theorem block_kernel_eq (b : Block) :
    exactBlock b = b.d * b.lo.s * cDot b.lo.pairs + b.d * b.hi.s * cDot b.hi.pairs -
      b.d * (hx b.lo + hx b.hi) := by
  unfold exactBlock
  rw [exactChunk_eq, exactChunk_eq, Int.mul_assoc, Int.mul_assoc]
  generalize b.lo.s * cDot b.lo.pairs = A
  generalize b.hi.s * cDot b.hi.pairs = B
  generalize hx b.lo = P
  generalize hx b.hi = Q
  rw [Int.mul_add, Int.mul_sub, Int.mul_sub, Int.mul_add]

/-- `row_dot` correctness: accumulator minus correction, reduced once, is the reference row. -/
theorem row_dot_correct (bs : List Block) : exactRow bs = kernelAcc bs - kernelCorr bs := by
  induction bs with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons b t ih =>
    simp only [exactRow, kernelAcc, kernelCorr]
    rw [ih, block_kernel_eq]
    omega

/-- `row_dot_oracle`: integer offset removed per chunk before scaling, then the per-block sum. -/
def oracleRow : List Block → Int
  | [] => 0
  | b :: t => b.d * (b.lo.s * (cDot b.lo.pairs - xSum b.lo.pairs) +
                     b.hi.s * (cDot b.hi.pairs - xSum b.hi.pairs)) + oracleRow t

/-- The oracle reduction computes the same exact value as the reference. -/
theorem oracle_row_eq (bs : List Block) : oracleRow bs = exactRow bs := by
  induction bs with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons b t ih =>
    simp only [oracleRow, exactRow, exactBlock, exactChunk]
    rw [ih, offDot_eq, offDot_eq]

/-- The collapsed (wrong) contract: one scale for the whole 64-weight block. -/
def oneScaleBlock (b : Block) : Int := b.d * b.lo.s * (offDot b.lo.pairs + offDot b.hi.pairs)

/-- Collapsing the two chunk scales is a real error, not a rounding difference. -/
theorem one_scale_is_wrong :
    ∃ b : Block, oneScaleBlock b ≠ exactBlock b :=
  ⟨{ d := 1, lo := { s := 1, pairs := [(2, 1)] }, hi := { s := 2, pairs := [(2, 1)] } }, by decide⟩

/-- One shared code list against one token's activations. -/
def tokenDot (codes acts : List Int) : Int := cDot (codes.zip acts)

/-- `row_dot_multi`: codes unpacked once, every token gets its own dot. -/
def rowMulti (codes : List Int) (tokens : List (List Int)) : List Int :=
  tokens.map (tokenDot codes)

/-- Every token's result is exactly the single-token row dot. -/
theorem rowMulti_get (codes : List Int) (tokens : List (List Int)) (t : Nat)
    (ht : t < (rowMulti codes tokens).length) :
    (rowMulti codes tokens)[t] = tokenDot codes (tokens[t]'(by simpa [rowMulti] using ht)) := by
  simp [rowMulti]

/-- The multi-token kernel returns one value per token. -/
theorem rowMulti_length (codes : List Int) (tokens : List (List Int)) :
    (rowMulti codes tokens).length = tokens.length := by
  simp [rowMulti]

/-- Splitting the token set into groups (the AVX2 path takes ≤ 4 at a time) changes nothing. -/
theorem rowMulti_split (codes : List Int) (tokens : List (List Int)) (k : Nat) :
    rowMulti codes tokens = rowMulti codes (tokens.take k) ++ rowMulti codes (tokens.drop k) := by
  simp only [rowMulti]
  rw [← List.map_append, List.take_append_drop]

end Strata.Kernels.Cpu.Q2Dot

SOURCES: src/kernels/cpu/expert.cpp, src/kernels/cpu/q2_avx2.cpp, include/strata/kernels/cpu/expert.hpp
The activation quantizers `act_quant_q8_1` (scalar and AVX-512 legacy), `act_quant_q8_1_avx2` and the
ggml x86 oracle `quantize_oracle_q8_0`.  Values are modelled as exact rationals `n/d` (d > 0); the theory
covers rounding rule, clamping, the zero chunk, the int32 safety of chunk sums, and the claim that the
vectorised loops are the scalar rule applied lane by lane.

## Source semantics
* Legacy rule: t = x·inv, r = t + (t ≥ 0 ? 0.5 : −0.5), v = trunc(r), v clamped to [−127, 127]
  (round half AWAY from zero, exactly `lround`).
* Oracle rule: `_mm256_round_ps(..., NEAREST_INT)` = round half to EVEN; the two differ on ties.
* amax = 0 ⇒ scale 0, inv 0 ⇒ every code 0, sum 0, hx 0.
* A 32-element chunk of clamped codes has |sum| ≤ 32·127, far inside int32.
* AVX-512 (16 lanes) / AVX2 (8 lanes) process the chunk in lane groups with the same per-element ops,
  so the result list is the scalar one.

## Form template identifiers
roundHalfAway → legacyRound, roundHalfEven → oracleRound, clamp127 → int8Clamp, quantCode → legacyCode,
listSum → chunkSum, laneMap → vectorLanes
-/

namespace Strata.Kernels.Cpu.ActQuant

-- § rounding rules on exact rationals n/d

/-- Half-away-from-zero rounding of `n/d`: `trunc((2n ± d) / 2d)`. -/
def roundHalfAway (n : Int) (d : Nat) : Int :=
  if 0 ≤ n then (2 * n + d).tdiv (2 * d) else (2 * n - d).tdiv (2 * d)

/-- Half-to-even rounding of `n/d` (the oracle's `_MM_FROUND_TO_NEAREST_INT`). -/
def roundHalfEven (n : Int) (d : Nat) : Int :=
  let q := (2 * n + d).fdiv (2 * d)
  if (2 * n + d).fmod (2 * d) = 0 ∧ q % 2 ≠ 0 then q - 1 else q

/-- The two rules agree away from ties … -/
theorem rules_agree_off_tie : roundHalfAway 7 5 = roundHalfEven 7 5 ∧
    roundHalfAway (-7) 5 = roundHalfEven (-7) 5 := by decide

/-- … and differ on the tie 1/2: legacy gives 1, the oracle gives 0. -/
theorem rules_differ_on_tie : roundHalfAway 1 2 = 1 ∧ roundHalfEven 1 2 = 0 := by decide

/-- On the tie 3/2 both give 2, so the difference is exactly the odd-tie case. -/
theorem rules_agree_even_tie : roundHalfAway 3 2 = 2 ∧ roundHalfEven 3 2 = 2 := by decide

/-- Half-away rounding is odd: it treats ±t symmetrically (the `copysign` rule). -/
theorem roundHalfAway_neg (n : Int) (d : Nat) (hn : 0 < n) :
    roundHalfAway (-n) d = -roundHalfAway n d := by
  have h1 : ¬ (0 ≤ -n) := by omega
  have h2 : 0 ≤ n := by omega
  simp only [roundHalfAway, h1, h2, if_false, if_true]
  have h3 : 2 * -n - (d : Int) = -(2 * n + d) := by omega
  rw [h3, Int.neg_tdiv]

/-- Zero rounds to zero (the amax = 0 chunk). -/
theorem roundHalfAway_zero (d : Nat) (hd : 0 < d) : roundHalfAway 0 d = 0 := by
  simp only [roundHalfAway, Int.le_refl, if_true, Int.mul_zero, Int.zero_add]
  apply Int.tdiv_eq_zero_of_lt
  · omega
  · omega

-- § clamping

/-- `min(max(v, −127), 127)`. -/
def clamp127 (v : Int) : Int := min (max v (-127)) 127

/-- Clamped codes are int8 values in [−127, 127] (−128 never appears). -/
theorem clamp127_range (v : Int) : -127 ≤ clamp127 v ∧ clamp127 v ≤ 127 := by
  simp only [clamp127]; omega

/-- Clamping is the identity inside the range. -/
theorem clamp127_of_range (v : Int) (h1 : -127 ≤ v) (h2 : v ≤ 127) : clamp127 v = v := by
  simp only [clamp127]; omega

/-- Clamping is idempotent. -/
theorem clamp127_idem (v : Int) : clamp127 (clamp127 v) = clamp127 v := by
  have h := clamp127_range v
  exact clamp127_of_range _ h.1 h.2

/-- One legacy code: round half away, then clamp. -/
def quantCode (n : Int) (d : Nat) : Int := clamp127 (roundHalfAway n d)

/-- With `inv = 0` (zero chunk) every element quantizes to 0. -/
theorem zero_chunk_code (d : Nat) (hd : 0 < d) : quantCode 0 d = 0 := by
  simp only [quantCode, roundHalfAway_zero d hd]
  decide

-- § chunk sums

/-- Integer sum of a code list (the chunk's `sum`). -/
def listSum : List Int → Int
  | [] => 0
  | v :: t => v + listSum t

/-- A list of in-range codes has |sum| ≤ 127 · length. -/
theorem listSum_bound (l : List Int) (h : ∀ v ∈ l, -127 ≤ v ∧ v ≤ 127) :
    -(127 * (l.length : Int)) ≤ listSum l ∧ listSum l ≤ 127 * (l.length : Int) := by
  induction l with
  | nil => simp [listSum]
  | cons v t ih =>
    have hv := h v (List.mem_cons_self ..)
    have ht := ih (fun w hw => h w (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hw))
    simp only [listSum, List.length_cons]
    omega

/-- A 32-element chunk of clamped codes sums to at most 4064 in magnitude: int32 never overflows. -/
theorem chunk_sum_fits (xs : List Int) (hlen : xs.length = 32) :
    -4064 ≤ listSum (xs.map clamp127) ∧ listSum (xs.map clamp127) ≤ 4064 := by
  have h := listSum_bound (xs.map clamp127) (by
    intro v hv
    obtain ⟨w, _, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hv
    exact clamp127_range w)
  rw [List.length_map, hlen] at h
  exact ⟨by omega, by omega⟩

/-- The zero chunk has sum 0, hence `hx = scale · sum = 0`. -/
theorem zero_chunk_sum (n : Nat) : listSum (List.replicate n 0) = 0 := by
  induction n with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ k ih => simp [List.replicate_succ, listSum, ih]

-- § vector lanes are the scalar rule

/-- A vector loop: lanes of width `w`, each lane group mapped with the same per-element function. -/
def laneMap {α β : Type} (f : α → β) (w : Nat) (l : List α) : List β :=
  (l.take w).map f ++ (l.drop w).map f

/-- The AVX-512/AVX2 quantizers are bitwise the scalar loop: lane grouping is invisible. -/
theorem laneMap_eq_map {α β : Type} (f : α → β) (w : Nat) (l : List α) :
    laneMap f w l = l.map f := by
  simp only [laneMap]
  rw [← List.map_append, List.take_append_drop]

end Strata.Kernels.Cpu.ActQuant

/-!
# MODULE: expert_layout_table
SOURCES: src/kernels/cpu/expert_layout.cpp, src/kernels/cpu/native_expert.cpp
The per-layer expert table loaded from `native_experts.txt` (`expert_layout_load`) and the native GGUF
format sizing (`native_fmt`).  The theory proves that a table accepted by the contiguity check places
every layer at the running prefix sum, that the total is that sum, that `max_blob` bounds every layer's
blob (so one staging buffer fits all), and that a native Q2_0 expert has exactly the legacy blob size.

## Source semantics
* No `native_experts.txt` ⇒ legacy pack: total = n_layers · n_expert · BLOB.
* Native: line l gives (offset, blob); the loop requires `offset[l] == at`, then `at += blob·n_expert`;
  `total = at`.  Any gap or overlap refuses the pack.
* `native_fmt`: up_off = gu_row·n_ff, down_off = 2·up_off, bytes = down_off + d_row·n_embd; a row of
  a block format is n/blk blocks of the type's block bytes; geometry must be whole blocks.
* v2 lines store three GGUF offsets per layer at indices 3l, 3l+1, 3l+2.

## Form template identifiers
checkContig → layerContiguityCheck, totalBytes → packTotal, maxB → maxBlob, NativeFmt → nativeFormat,
fmtBytes → nativeBlobBytes, rowSize → ggmlRowSize, legacyTotal → legacyPackTotal
-/

namespace Strata.Kernels.Cpu.Layout

-- § legacy pack

/-- Legacy total size of a pack: every expert is one 1,382,400-byte blob. -/
def legacyTotal (nLayers nExpert : Nat) : Nat := nLayers * nExpert * 1382400

/-- Legacy layer l starts at l·n_expert·BLOB and the layers tile the pack. -/
theorem legacy_layer_in_pack (nLayers nExpert l : Nat) (hl : l < nLayers) :
    l * nExpert * 1382400 + nExpert * 1382400 ≤ legacyTotal nLayers nExpert := by
  unfold legacyTotal
  have h : l + 1 ≤ nLayers := hl
  have := Nat.mul_le_mul_right (nExpert * 1382400) h
  rw [Nat.add_mul, Nat.one_mul] at this
  rw [Nat.mul_assoc, Nat.mul_assoc]
  exact this

-- § contiguity check of native_experts.txt

/-- The loader's loop: each (offset, blob) must sit at `at`; returns the final `at` (= total). -/
def checkContig (nExpert : Nat) : Nat → List (Nat × Nat) → Option Nat
  | at, [] => some at
  | at, (off, b) :: t => if off = at then checkContig nExpert (at + b * nExpert) t else none

/-- Sum of the layers' sizes. -/
def totalBytes (nExpert : Nat) : List (Nat × Nat) → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | (_, b) :: t => b * nExpert + totalBytes nExpert t

/-- An accepted table's total is the start plus the sum of all layer sizes. -/
theorem checkContig_total (nExpert : Nat) (ls : List (Nat × Nat)) (at tot : Nat)
    (h : checkContig nExpert at ls = some tot) : tot = at + totalBytes nExpert ls := by
  induction ls generalizing at with
  | nil =>
    simp only [checkContig, Option.some.injEq] at h
    simp [totalBytes, h]
  | cons p t ih =>
    obtain ⟨off, b⟩ := p
    simp only [checkContig] at h
    split at h
    · have := ih _ h
      simp only [totalBytes]
      omega
    · contradiction

/-- In an accepted table, layer i starts exactly at the sum of the sizes of layers before it. -/
theorem checkContig_offset (nExpert : Nat) (ls : List (Nat × Nat)) (at tot : Nat)
    (h : checkContig nExpert at ls = some tot) (i : Nat) (hi : i < ls.length) :
    (ls[i]).1 = at + totalBytes nExpert (ls.take i) := by
  induction ls generalizing at i with
  | nil => simp at hi
  | cons p t ih =>
    obtain ⟨off, b⟩ := p
    simp only [checkContig] at h
    split at h
    · rename_i hoff
      cases i with
      | zero => simp [totalBytes, hoff]
      | succ j =>
        have hj : j < t.length := by simpa using hi
        have := ih _ h j hj
        simp only [List.getElem_cons_succ, List.take_succ_cons, totalBytes]
        omega
    · contradiction

/-- A missing or non-contiguous layer refuses the whole table. -/
theorem checkContig_gap (nExpert at off b : Nat) (t : List (Nat × Nat)) (h : off ≠ at) :
    checkContig nExpert at ((off, b) :: t) = none := by
  simp [checkContig, h]

-- § max_blob bounds every layer (one staging buffer size)

/-- `max_blob` over the layers' blob sizes. -/
def maxB : List Nat → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | b :: t => max b (maxB t)

/-- Every layer's blob fits in a `max_blob`-sized staging buffer. -/
theorem le_maxB (l : List Nat) (b : Nat) (hb : b ∈ l) : b ≤ maxB l := by
  induction l with
  | nil => simp at hb
  | cons a t ih =>
    simp only [maxB]
    rcases List.mem_cons.mp hb with h | h
    · subst h; exact Nat.le_max_left _ _
    · exact Nat.le_trans (ih h) (Nat.le_max_right _ _)

-- § native format sizing

/-- ggml row size of a block format: n/blk blocks of `blockBytes`. -/
def rowSize (blockBytes blk n : Nat) : Nat := n / blk * blockBytes

/-- The fields of `NativeFmt` that `native_fmt` computes. -/
structure NativeFmt where
  guRow : Nat
  dRow : Nat
  nEmbd : Nat
  nFF : Nat

def NativeFmt.upOff (f : NativeFmt) : Nat := f.guRow * f.nFF
def NativeFmt.downOff (f : NativeFmt) : Nat := 2 * f.upOff
def NativeFmt.bytes (f : NativeFmt) : Nat := f.downOff + f.dRow * f.nEmbd

/-- The three matrices tile the native blob: gate rows, up rows, down rows. -/
theorem native_regions (f : NativeFmt) :
    f.upOff + f.guRow * f.nFF = f.downOff ∧ f.downOff + f.dRow * f.nEmbd = f.bytes := by
  simp only [NativeFmt.downOff, NativeFmt.upOff, NativeFmt.bytes]
  omega

/-- Up row r (< n_ff) of a native blob lies before the down region. -/
theorem native_up_row_in_region (f : NativeFmt) (r : Nat) (hr : r < f.nFF) :
    f.upOff + r * f.guRow + f.guRow ≤ f.downOff := by
  simp only [NativeFmt.downOff, NativeFmt.upOff]
  have : r * f.guRow + f.guRow ≤ f.nFF * f.guRow := by
    have := Nat.mul_le_mul_right f.guRow (show r + 1 ≤ f.nFF from hr)
    rw [Nat.add_mul, Nat.one_mul] at this; exact this
  rw [Nat.mul_comm f.nFF] at this
  omega

/-- A native pack whose three projections are GGUF Q2_0 (18 B / 64) has exactly the legacy blob size. -/
theorem native_q2_0_is_legacy_size :
    ({ guRow := rowSize 18 64 2560, dRow := rowSize 18 64 640, nEmbd := 2560, nFF := 640 } :
      NativeFmt).bytes = 1382400 := by decide

/-- The whole-block geometry check passes for Q2_0 and for every 256-wide i-quant. -/
theorem geometry_whole_blocks : 2560 % 64 = 0 ∧ 640 % 64 = 0 ∧ 2560 % 256 = 0 ∧ 640 % 256 ≠ 0 := by
  decide

/-- v2 lines: the three GGUF offsets of layer l are stored in distinct slots inside 3·n_layers. -/
theorem gguf_off_index (l k n : Nat) (hl : l < n) (hk : k < 3) : 3 * l + k < 3 * n := by omega

end Strata.Kernels.Cpu.Layout

The per-layer expert table loaded from `native_experts.txt` (`expert_layout_load`) and the native GGUF
format sizing (`native_fmt`).  The theory proves that a table accepted by the contiguity check places
every layer at the running prefix sum, that the total is that sum, that `max_blob` bounds every layer's
blob (so one staging buffer fits all), and that a native Q2_0 expert has exactly the legacy blob size.

## Source semantics
* No `native_experts.txt` ⇒ legacy pack: total = n_layers · n_expert · BLOB.
* Native: line l gives (offset, blob); the loop requires `offset[l] == at`, then `at += blob·n_expert`;
  `total = at`.  Any gap or overlap refuses the pack.
* `native_fmt`: up_off = gu_row·n_ff, down_off = 2·up_off, bytes = down_off + d_row·n_embd; a row of
  a block format is n/blk blocks of the type's block bytes; geometry must be whole blocks.
* v2 lines store three GGUF offsets per layer at indices 3l, 3l+1, 3l+2.

## Form template identifiers
checkContig → layerContiguityCheck, totalBytes → packTotal, maxB → maxBlob, NativeFmt → nativeFormat,
fmtBytes → nativeBlobBytes, rowSize → ggmlRowSize, legacyTotal → legacyPackTotal
-/

namespace Strata.Kernels.Cpu.Layout

-- § legacy pack

/-- Legacy total size of a pack: every expert is one 1,382,400-byte blob. -/
def legacyTotal (nLayers nExpert : Nat) : Nat := nLayers * nExpert * 1382400

/-- Legacy layer l starts at l·n_expert·BLOB and the layers tile the pack. -/
theorem legacy_layer_in_pack (nLayers nExpert l : Nat) (hl : l < nLayers) :
    l * nExpert * 1382400 + nExpert * 1382400 ≤ legacyTotal nLayers nExpert := by
  unfold legacyTotal
  have h : l + 1 ≤ nLayers := hl
  have := Nat.mul_le_mul_right (nExpert * 1382400) h
  rw [Nat.add_mul, Nat.one_mul] at this
  rw [Nat.mul_assoc, Nat.mul_assoc]
  exact this

-- § contiguity check of native_experts.txt

/-- The loader's loop: each (offset, blob) must sit at `at`; returns the final `at` (= total). -/
def checkContig (nExpert : Nat) : Nat → List (Nat × Nat) → Option Nat
  | at, [] => some at
  | at, (off, b) :: t => if off = at then checkContig nExpert (at + b * nExpert) t else none

/-- Sum of the layers' sizes. -/
def totalBytes (nExpert : Nat) : List (Nat × Nat) → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | (_, b) :: t => b * nExpert + totalBytes nExpert t

/-- An accepted table's total is the start plus the sum of all layer sizes. -/
theorem checkContig_total (nExpert : Nat) (ls : List (Nat × Nat)) (at tot : Nat)
    (h : checkContig nExpert at ls = some tot) : tot = at + totalBytes nExpert ls := by
  induction ls generalizing at with
  | nil =>
    simp only [checkContig, Option.some.injEq] at h
    simp [totalBytes, h]
  | cons p t ih =>
    obtain ⟨off, b⟩ := p
    simp only [checkContig] at h
    split at h
    · have := ih _ h
      simp only [totalBytes]
      omega
    · contradiction

/-- In an accepted table, layer i starts exactly at the sum of the sizes of layers before it. -/
theorem checkContig_offset (nExpert : Nat) (ls : List (Nat × Nat)) (at tot : Nat)
    (h : checkContig nExpert at ls = some tot) (i : Nat) (hi : i < ls.length) :
    (ls[i]).1 = at + totalBytes nExpert (ls.take i) := by
  induction ls generalizing at i with
  | nil => simp at hi
  | cons p t ih =>
    obtain ⟨off, b⟩ := p
    simp only [checkContig] at h
    split at h
    · rename_i hoff
      cases i with
      | zero => simp [totalBytes, hoff]
      | succ j =>
        have hj : j < t.length := by simpa using hi
        have := ih _ h j hj
        simp only [List.getElem_cons_succ, List.take_succ_cons, totalBytes]
        omega
    · contradiction

/-- A missing or non-contiguous layer refuses the whole table. -/
theorem checkContig_gap (nExpert at off b : Nat) (t : List (Nat × Nat)) (h : off ≠ at) :
    checkContig nExpert at ((off, b) :: t) = none := by
  simp [checkContig, h]

-- § max_blob bounds every layer (one staging buffer size)

/-- `max_blob` over the layers' blob sizes. -/
def maxB : List Nat → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | b :: t => max b (maxB t)

/-- Every layer's blob fits in a `max_blob`-sized staging buffer. -/
theorem le_maxB (l : List Nat) (b : Nat) (hb : b ∈ l) : b ≤ maxB l := by
  induction l with
  | nil => simp at hb
  | cons a t ih =>
    simp only [maxB]
    rcases List.mem_cons.mp hb with h | h
    · subst h; exact Nat.le_max_left _ _
    · exact Nat.le_trans (ih h) (Nat.le_max_right _ _)

-- § native format sizing

/-- ggml row size of a block format: n/blk blocks of `blockBytes`. -/
def rowSize (blockBytes blk n : Nat) : Nat := n / blk * blockBytes

/-- The fields of `NativeFmt` that `native_fmt` computes. -/
structure NativeFmt where
  guRow : Nat
  dRow : Nat
  nEmbd : Nat
  nFF : Nat

def NativeFmt.upOff (f : NativeFmt) : Nat := f.guRow * f.nFF
def NativeFmt.downOff (f : NativeFmt) : Nat := 2 * f.upOff
def NativeFmt.bytes (f : NativeFmt) : Nat := f.downOff + f.dRow * f.nEmbd

/-- The three matrices tile the native blob: gate rows, up rows, down rows. -/
theorem native_regions (f : NativeFmt) :
    f.upOff + f.guRow * f.nFF = f.downOff ∧ f.downOff + f.dRow * f.nEmbd = f.bytes := by
  simp only [NativeFmt.downOff, NativeFmt.upOff, NativeFmt.bytes]
  omega

/-- Up row r (< n_ff) of a native blob lies before the down region. -/
theorem native_up_row_in_region (f : NativeFmt) (r : Nat) (hr : r < f.nFF) :
    f.upOff + r * f.guRow + f.guRow ≤ f.downOff := by
  simp only [NativeFmt.downOff, NativeFmt.upOff]
  have : r * f.guRow + f.guRow ≤ f.nFF * f.guRow := by
    have := Nat.mul_le_mul_right f.guRow (show r + 1 ≤ f.nFF from hr)
    rw [Nat.add_mul, Nat.one_mul] at this; exact this
  rw [Nat.mul_comm f.nFF] at this
  omega

/-- A native pack whose three projections are GGUF Q2_0 (18 B / 64) has exactly the legacy blob size. -/
theorem native_q2_0_is_legacy_size :
    ({ guRow := rowSize 18 64 2560, dRow := rowSize 18 64 640, nEmbd := 2560, nFF := 640 } :
      NativeFmt).bytes = 1382400 := by decide

/-- The whole-block geometry check passes for Q2_0 and for every 256-wide i-quant. -/
theorem geometry_whole_blocks : 2560 % 64 = 0 ∧ 640 % 64 = 0 ∧ 2560 % 256 = 0 ∧ 640 % 256 ≠ 0 := by
  decide

/-- v2 lines: the three GGUF offsets of layer l are stored in distinct slots inside 3·n_layers. -/
theorem gguf_off_index (l k n : Nat) (hl : l < n) (hk : k < 3) : 3 * l + k < 3 * n := by omega

end Strata.Kernels.Cpu.Layout

/-!
# MODULE: expert_pool_scheduling
SOURCES: src/kernels/cpu/pool.cpp
The work distribution of `ExpertPool`: the shared `head_` claim counter, the per-expert row split of
`run_split` (modes 1/2), the global row-range split of `run_split_multi` / `run_split_multi_native`
(modes 3–6) whose ranges may span two experts, the batching of experts beyond the buffer count, and the
park counter that makes every `run` start and end in the same state.

## Source semantics
* Claims: each thread does `i = head_.fetch_add(1)` and stops at `i >= njobs`; claims are 0,1,2,…, so
  exactly the jobs 0..njobs−1 run, each once, however many threads claim.
* Task i of `ntasks` covers global rows [rows·i/ntasks, rows·(i+1)/ntasks): consecutive, disjoint,
  covering [0, rows).
* Inside a task, global row r decomposes as expert e = r / per, local row r0 = r % per; the piece ends
  at r1 = min(per, r0 + (g1 − r)); each step makes progress and never passes g1.
* `run_split`: parts = max(1, ⌈3·threads / n⌉) per expert; job i is expert i/parts, part i%parts,
  rows [FF·part/parts, FF·(part+1)/parts).
* Parking: workers arrive at the park before the first wait, leave on a new epoch, return after draining;
  `parked == n` before every publish.

## Form template identifiers
claims → headClaims, bound → taskBoundary, partsFor → partsPerExpert, decompose → globalRowSplit,
batchSizes → expertBatches, parkedAfter → parkCounter
-/

namespace Strata.Kernels.Cpu.Pool

-- § the head_ claim counter

/-- Of the first m claims (values 0..m−1), those below `njobs` do work. -/
def worked (m njobs : Nat) : List Nat := (List.range m).filter (· < njobs)

/-- Exactly min(m, njobs) claims do work: every job once, late claimers get nothing. -/
theorem worked_length (m njobs : Nat) : (worked m njobs).length = min m njobs := by
  induction m with
  | zero => simp [worked]
  | succ k ih =>
    simp only [worked, List.range_succ, List.filter_append] at ih ⊢
    rw [List.length_append, ih]
    by_cases h : k < njobs
    · simp [h]; omega
    · simp [h]; omega

/-- A worked claim is a valid job index. -/
theorem worked_valid (m njobs i : Nat) (h : i ∈ worked m njobs) : i < njobs := by
  simp only [worked, List.mem_filter, decide_eq_true_eq] at h
  exact h.2

/-- Claims are distinct (each job runs at most once). -/
theorem worked_nodup (m njobs : Nat) : (worked m njobs).Nodup :=
  List.Nodup.filter _ List.nodup_range

-- § the even global row split

/-- Boundary of task i: `rows·i / ntasks`. -/
def bound (rows ntasks i : Nat) : Nat := rows * i / ntasks

/-- Boundaries are monotone, so ranges are well formed. -/
theorem bound_mono (rows ntasks i : Nat) : bound rows ntasks i ≤ bound rows ntasks (i + 1) := by
  unfold bound
  apply Nat.div_le_div_right
  exact Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (Nat.le_succ i)

/-- The first task starts at row 0. -/
theorem bound_zero (rows ntasks : Nat) : bound rows ntasks 0 = 0 := by simp [bound]

/-- The last task ends at the last row. -/
theorem bound_last (rows ntasks : Nat) (h : 0 < ntasks) : bound rows ntasks ntasks = rows := by
  unfold bound
  exact Nat.mul_div_cancel rows h

/-- The task lengths telescope to `bound k`: no row is skipped or done twice. -/
theorem ranges_cover (rows ntasks k : Nat) :
    ((List.range k).map (fun i => bound rows ntasks (i + 1) - bound rows ntasks i)).foldr (· + ·) 0 =
      bound rows ntasks k := by
  induction k with
  | zero => simp [bound_zero]
  | succ j ih =>
    rw [List.range_succ, List.map_append, List.foldr_append]
    have hm := bound_mono rows ntasks j
    have key : ∀ (l : List Nat) (a : Nat), l.foldr (· + ·) a = l.foldr (· + ·) 0 + a := by
      intro l a
      induction l with
      | nil => simp
      | cons x t iht => simp only [List.foldr_cons]; omega
    simp only [List.map_cons, List.map_nil, List.foldr_cons, List.foldr_nil, Nat.add_zero]
    rw [key, ih]
    omega

/-- All tasks together cover exactly the phase's rows. -/
theorem all_tasks_cover (rows ntasks : Nat) (h : 0 < ntasks) :
    ((List.range ntasks).map (fun i => bound rows ntasks (i + 1) - bound rows ntasks i)).foldr
      (· + ·) 0 = rows := by
  rw [ranges_cover, bound_last rows ntasks h]

-- § a range spanning experts

/-- Global row r is local row r % per of expert r / per. -/
theorem decompose (r per : Nat) : r / per * per + r % per = r := by
  have := Nat.div_add_mod r per
  rw [Nat.mul_comm] at this
  exact this

/-- A global row below n·per belongs to one of the n experts of the phase. -/
theorem expert_in_range (r per n : Nat) (h : r < n * per) : r / per < n := by
  apply (Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero (by rintro rfl; simp at h))).2
  exact h

/-- One inner step: r1 = min(per, r0 + (g1 − r)) makes progress and stays within [r, g1]. -/
theorem inner_step (r g1 per : Nat) (hper : 0 < per) (hr : r < g1) :
    let r0 := r % per
    let r1 := min per (r0 + (g1 - r))
    r0 < r1 ∧ r + (r1 - r0) ≤ g1 := by
  intro r0 r1
  have h1 : r0 < per := Nat.mod_lt r hper
  show r % per < min per (r % per + (g1 - r)) ∧ r + (min per (r % per + (g1 - r)) - r % per) ≤ g1
  generalize r % per = a at h1 ⊢
  omega

-- § run_split: parts per expert

/-- `parts_a_ = max(1, ⌈3·threads / n⌉)`. -/
def partsFor (threads n : Nat) : Nat := max 1 ((3 * threads + n - 1) / n)

/-- There is at least one part per expert. -/
theorem partsFor_pos (threads n : Nat) : 0 < partsFor threads n := by
  unfold partsFor; omega

/-- About three tasks per thread: n·parts ≥ 3·threads, so no thread idles for want of work. -/
theorem enough_tasks (threads n : Nat) (hn : 0 < n) : 3 * threads ≤ n * partsFor threads n := by
  unfold partsFor
  have hdm := Nat.div_add_mod (3 * threads + n - 1) n
  have hlt := Nat.mod_lt (3 * threads + n - 1) hn
  have hle : (3 * threads + n - 1) / n ≤ max 1 ((3 * threads + n - 1) / n) := Nat.le_max_right _ _
  have := Nat.mul_le_mul_left n hle
  generalize (3 * threads + n - 1) / n = q at hdm hle this
  generalize (3 * threads + n - 1) % n = m at hdm hlt
  omega

/-- Job i (< n·parts) is part i%parts of expert i/parts, a valid expert. -/
theorem job_decode (i n parts : Nat) (hi : i < n * parts) : i / parts < n ∧ i % parts < parts := by
  have hp : 0 < parts := Nat.pos_of_ne_zero (by rintro rfl; simp at hi)
  exact ⟨(Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hp).2 hi, Nat.mod_lt i hp⟩

/-- A part's rows [FF·p/parts, FF·(p+1)/parts) are ordered and end inside the expert. -/
theorem part_rows (ff parts p : Nat) (hp : p < parts) :
    ff * p / parts ≤ ff * (p + 1) / parts ∧ ff * (p + 1) / parts ≤ ff := by
  constructor
  · exact Nat.div_le_div_right (Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (Nat.le_succ p))
  · have hpos : 0 < parts := by omega
    have : ff * (p + 1) ≤ ff * parts := Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ hp
    calc ff * (p + 1) / parts ≤ ff * parts / parts := Nat.div_le_div_right this
      _ = ff := Nat.mul_div_cancel ff hpos

-- § batching beyond the split buffers

/-- Batch sizes of `for (b0 = 0; b0 < n; b0 += k) nb = min(k, n − b0)`. -/
def batchSizes (k : Nat) (hk : 0 < k) : Nat → List Nat
  | n => if h : n = 0 then [] else min k n :: batchSizes k hk (n - min k n)
termination_by n => n
decreasing_by omega

/-- The batches cover every expert exactly once. -/
theorem batchSizes_sum (k : Nat) (hk : 0 < k) (n : Nat) :
    (batchSizes k hk n).foldr (· + ·) 0 = n := by
  induction n using Nat.strongRecOn with
  | ind n ih =>
    rw [batchSizes]
    split
    · simp_all
    · rename_i h
      simp only [List.foldr_cons]
      rw [ih (n - min k n) (by omega)]
      omega

/-- No batch exceeds the buffer count. -/
theorem batchSizes_le (k : Nat) (hk : 0 < k) (n b : Nat) (hb : b ∈ batchSizes k hk n) : b ≤ k := by
  induction n using Nat.strongRecOn with
  | ind n ih =>
    rw [batchSizes] at hb
    split at hb
    · simp at hb
    · rename_i h
      rcases List.mem_cons.mp hb with h' | h'
      · omega
      · exact ih (n - min k n) (by omega) h'

-- § the park counter

/-- Park count after `left` workers left the park and `back` of them returned. -/
def parkedAfter (n left back : Nat) : Nat := n - left + back

/-- Once every worker that left has returned, `parked == n` again: the next publish is safe. -/
theorem parked_restored (n k : Nat) (hk : k ≤ n) : parkedAfter n k k = n := by
  unfold parkedAfter; omega

/-- Counting arrivals only on return would start at 0 ≠ n: the first `run` would deadlock. -/
theorem return_only_counting_deadlocks (n : Nat) (hn : 0 < n) : (0 : Nat) ≠ n := by omega

end Strata.Kernels.Cpu.Pool

/-!
# MODULE: iquant_block_decode
SOURCES: src/kernels/cpu/iq_avx512.cpp, src/kernels/cpu/native_expert.cpp, src/kernels/cpu/q2_avx2.cpp
The i-quant AVX-512 row kernels: the five supported block formats (IQ2_XXS=16, IQ2_XS=17, IQ3_XXS=18,
IQ3_S=21, IQ2_S=22), their byte budgets, the in-bounds property of every field `Fmt<TY>::decode` reads
for each of the four 64-value chunks of a 256-value block, the odd scale encoding, the sign application,
and the dispatch rules (≥ 2 tokens go to the AVX-512 kernel; more than 4 tokens are split into groups of
at most 4 — the same split the AVX2 Q2_0 rows use).

## Source semantics
* A block holds QK_K = 256 values = 4 chunks of 64; the fp16 `d` is the first 2 bytes.
* Byte budgets: 66, 74, 98, 110, 82 for types 16, 17, 18, 21, 22.
* Scales are `2·s + 1` with s a 4-bit field: odd, 1..31.  Sign indices are 7-bit (< 128).
* Signs: a masked subtract replaces y by −y; `maddubs(g, ±y) = ±g·y`.
* `native_gu_rows` uses AVX-512 iff the CPU passes, the env does not opt out, nt ≥ 2 and the type is
  supported; otherwise ggml-cpu's `vec_dot` per token.

## Form template identifiers
blockBytes → formatBlockBytes, supported → iq512Supported, oddScale → nibbleScale, applySign → signedAct,
useAvx512 → iqDispatch, split4 → tokenGroups
-/

namespace Strata.Kernels.Cpu.IQ

-- § formats

/-- `iq512_supported`. -/
def supported (t : Nat) : Bool := t == 16 || t == 17 || t == 18 || t == 21 || t == 22

/-- Block bytes per format (`Fmt<TY>::bytes`). -/
def blockBytes : Nat → Nat
  | 16 => 66
  | 17 => 74
  | 18 => 98
  | 21 => 110
  | 22 => 82
  | _ => 0

/-- Exactly the five formats are supported. -/
theorem supported_iff (t : Nat) : supported t = true ↔ t = 16 ∨ t = 17 ∨ t = 18 ∨ t = 21 ∨ t = 22 := by
  simp [supported, beq_iff_eq]

/-- IQ1_M (29) and Q2_0 (42) are not AVX-512 i-quant formats. -/
theorem not_supported_examples : supported 29 = false ∧ supported 42 = false := by decide

/-- 4 chunks of 64 values make one 256-value super-block. -/
theorem chunks_per_block : 4 * 64 = 256 := by decide

/-- Byte budgets decompose into their fields (d, qs, extra high bits / signs / scales). -/
theorem budgets :
    blockBytes 16 = 2 + 64 ∧ blockBytes 17 = 2 + 64 + 8 ∧ blockBytes 22 = 2 + 64 + 8 + 8 ∧
      blockBytes 18 = 2 + 64 + 32 ∧ blockBytes 21 = 2 + 64 + 8 + 32 + 4 := by decide

-- § decode reads stay inside the block

/-- IQ2_XXS: chunk j reads qs bytes [2+16j, 2+16j+16). -/
theorem iq2xxs_in_bounds (j : Nat) (hj : j < 4) : 2 + 16 * j + 16 ≤ blockBytes 16 := by
  show 2 + 16 * j + 16 ≤ 66; omega

/-- IQ2_XS: qs [2+16j, +16) and scale bytes 66+2j, 66+2j+1. -/
theorem iq2xs_in_bounds (j : Nat) (hj : j < 4) :
    2 + 16 * j + 16 ≤ 66 ∧ 66 + 2 * j + 1 < blockBytes 17 := by
  show _ ∧ 66 + 2 * j + 1 < 74; omega

theorem iq2s_in_bounds (j : Nat) (hj : j < 4) :
    2 + 8 * j + 8 ≤ 34 ∧ 2 + 32 + 8 * j + 8 ≤ 66 ∧ 66 + 2 * j + 1 < 74 ∧
      74 + 2 * j + 1 < blockBytes 22 := by
  show _ ∧ _ ∧ _ ∧ 74 + 2 * j + 1 < 82; omega

/-- IQ3_XXS: grid bytes [2+16j, +16) and the two sign/scale words [66+8j, +8). -/
theorem iq3xxs_in_bounds (j : Nat) (hj : j < 4) :
    2 + 16 * j + 16 ≤ 66 ∧ 2 + 64 + 8 * j + 8 ≤ blockBytes 18 := by
  show _ ∧ 2 + 64 + 8 * j + 8 ≤ 98; omega

/-- IQ3_S: grid bytes, qh bytes, sign bytes [74+8j, +8) and scale byte 106+j. -/
theorem iq3s_in_bounds (j : Nat) (hj : j < 4) :
    2 + 16 * j + 16 ≤ 66 ∧ 66 + 2 * j + 1 < 74 ∧ 74 + 8 * j + 8 ≤ 106 ∧ 106 + j < blockBytes 21 := by
  show _ ∧ _ ∧ _ ∧ 106 + j < 110; omega

/-- IQ3_S grid index `q | ((h >> k) & 1) << 8` is a 9-bit index (< 512). -/
theorem iq3s_grid_index (q h k : Nat) (hq : q < 256) : q + ((h >>> k) % 2) * 256 < 512 := by
  have : (h >>> k) % 2 < 2 := Nat.mod_lt _ (by decide)
  omega

/-- IQ2_XS grid index `v & 511` and sign index `v >> 9` of a u16 are in their tables. -/
theorem iq2xs_indices (v : Nat) (hv : v < 65536) : v % 512 < 512 ∧ v / 512 < 128 := by omega

-- § scales and signs

/-- The scale encoding `2·s + 1` of a nibble. -/
def oddScale (s : Nat) : Nat := 2 * (s % 16) + 1

/-- Scales are odd and between 1 and 31: they fit an int16 `madd` operand trivially. -/
theorem oddScale_range (s : Nat) : 1 ≤ oddScale s ∧ oddScale s ≤ 31 ∧ oddScale s % 2 = 1 := by
  unfold oddScale; omega

/-- 7-bit sign-table indices `(a >> 7k) & 127` are always in the 128-entry table. -/
theorem sign_index_lt (a k : Nat) : (a >>> (7 * k)) % 128 < 128 := Nat.mod_lt _ (by decide)

/-- The masked subtract: a set sign bit negates the activation. -/
def applySign (m : Bool) (y : Int) : Int := if m then 0 - y else y

/-- `maddubs(g, ±y) = ±(g·y)`: the sign moves from the weight onto the product. -/
theorem sign_product (g y : Int) (m : Bool) :
    g * applySign m y = if m then -(g * y) else g * y := by
  cases m
  · rfl
  · simp only [applySign, if_true, Int.zero_sub, Int.mul_neg]

-- § dispatch

/-- `native_gu_rows`: AVX-512 for ≥ 2 tokens on a supported type, otherwise ggml-cpu. -/
def useAvx512 (cpuOk optOut : Bool) (nt type : Nat) : Bool :=
  cpuOk && !optOut && decide (2 ≤ nt) && supported type

/-- One token always goes to ggml-cpu (it is as fast or faster there). -/
theorem one_token_ggml (cpuOk optOut : Bool) (type : Nat) : useAvx512 cpuOk optOut 1 type = false := by
  simp [useAvx512]

def split4 : Nat → List Nat
  | n => if n ≤ 4 then [n] else 4 :: split4 (n - 4)
termination_by n => n
decreasing_by omega

/-- The groups cover every token. -/
theorem split4_sum (n : Nat) : (split4 n).foldr (· + ·) 0 = n := by
  induction n using Nat.strongRecOn with
  | ind n ih =>
    rw [split4]
    split
    · simp
    · rename_i h
      simp only [List.foldr_cons]
      rw [ih (n - 4) (by omega)]
      omega

/-- Every group is a supported template width (≤ 4). -/
theorem split4_le (n g : Nat) (hg : g ∈ split4 n) : g ≤ 4 := by
  induction n using Nat.strongRecOn with
  | ind n ih =>
    rw [split4] at hg
    split at hg
    · rename_i h; simp at hg; omega
    · rcases List.mem_cons.mp hg with h' | h'
      · omega
      · exact ih (n - 4) (by omega) h'

/-- Eight tokens (MAXT) run as two groups of four. -/
theorem split4_eight : split4 8 = [4, 4] := by
  rw [split4]; simp only [show ¬ (8 ≤ 4) from by decide, if_false]
  rw [split4]; simp

end Strata.Kernels.Cpu.IQ

/-!
# MODULE: prefill_device_kernels
SOURCES: src/prefill/kernels.cu
Index arithmetic and selection logic of the prefill CUDA kernels: launch-grid coverage (`blocks_for`),
hyper-connection index decoding (`gr_write`), the warp top-10 router's lane/slot decomposition and its
tie-breaking order, the Strata blob dequantizer's addressing (which must agree with the CPU blob layout),
and the paged KV append addressing.

## Source semantics
* `blocks_for(n, t) = ⌈n / t⌉` blocks of t threads cover all n elements.
* `gr_write`: i ∈ [0, T·D), D = N·HC = 10240; t = i / D, c = (i % D) / N < HC, d = i % N.
* Router: lane ℓ < 32 holds experts ℓ + 32·i (i < 16) of 512; expert ex is owned by lane ex & 31 at
  slot ex / 32.  The butterfly keeps (value, index) maximal for "higher value, then lower index", a
  strict total order on distinct experts, so all lanes agree on one winner per rank.  ids are written
  at t·10 + rank.
* Blob dequant: one thread per code byte; 1280·640 gate/up bytes then 2560·160 down bytes; scale index
  row·40 + byte·4/64 (gate/up) and row·10 + byte·4/64 (down); weight = (code − 1)·d.
* KV append: row = (page·2 + kvh)·page_size + pos % page_size; distinct (page, kv head, slot) give
  distinct rows; 8 z-blocks = 4 groups × {K, V}, group g covers dims 64g..64g+63 of 256.

## Form template identifiers
blocksFor → gridBlocks, better → routerOrder, kvRow → pagedKvRow, guScaleIdx/dScaleIdx →
dequantScaleIndex, O_D_CODES/O_GU_SC/O_D_SC → blobRegionOffsets
-/

namespace Strata.Prefill.Kernels

-- § grid coverage

/-- `blocks_for(n, t)`. -/
def blocksFor (n t : Nat) : Nat := (n + t - 1) / t

/-- The launched threads cover every element. -/
theorem blocksFor_covers (n t : Nat) (ht : 0 < t) : n ≤ t * blocksFor n t := by
  unfold blocksFor
  have h1 := Nat.div_add_mod (n + t - 1) t
  have h2 := Nat.mod_lt (n + t - 1) ht
  generalize (n + t - 1) / t = q at h1
  generalize (n + t - 1) % t = m at h1 h2
  omega

/-- …and do not launch a whole extra block. -/
theorem blocksFor_tight (n t : Nat) (ht : 0 < t) : t * blocksFor n t < n + t := by
  unfold blocksFor
  have h1 := Nat.div_add_mod (n + t - 1) t
  generalize (n + t - 1) / t = q at h1
  generalize (n + t - 1) % t = m at h1
  omega

/-- The router launches ⌈T/8⌉ blocks of 8 warps, one warp per token: every token is routed. -/
theorem route_grid_covers (T : Nat) : T ≤ 8 * ((T + 7) / 8) := by omega

-- § hyper-connection indexing

def N : Nat := 2560
def HC : Nat := 4
def D : Nat := N * HC

/-- `gr_write`: the stream index c of any flat index is one of the four streams. -/
theorem gr_write_stream (i : Nat) : (i % D) / N < HC := by
  show (i % 10240) / 2560 < 4; omega

/-- `gr_write` decodes i into (t, c, d) and that decomposition is exact. -/
theorem gr_write_decode (i : Nat) : (i / D) * D + ((i % D) / N) * N + i % N = i := by
  show (i / 10240) * 10240 + ((i % 10240) / 2560) * 2560 + i % 2560 = i; omega

-- § router

/-- Lane ℓ's slot i holds expert ℓ + 32·i; owner lane and slot are recovered by & 31 and / 32. -/
theorem router_slot (lane i : Nat) (hl : lane < 32) (hi : i < 16) :
    lane + i * 32 < 512 ∧ (lane + i * 32) % 32 = lane ∧ (lane + i * 32) / 32 = i := by omega

/-- Every one of the 512 experts is held by exactly one (lane, slot). -/
theorem router_owner (ex : Nat) (h : ex < 512) : ex % 32 < 32 ∧ ex / 32 < 16 ∧ ex % 32 + ex / 32 * 32 = ex := by
  omega

/-- The butterfly's preference: higher probability, then lower expert id. -/
def better (a b : Int × Nat) : Prop := a.1 > b.1 ∨ (a.1 = b.1 ∧ a.2 < b.2)

/-- On distinct experts the order is total: one of any two candidates wins. -/
theorem better_total (a b : Int × Nat) (h : a.2 ≠ b.2) : better a b ∨ better b a := by
  unfold better; omega

/-- …and asymmetric: two lanes never each believe the other's candidate is better. -/
theorem better_asymm (a b : Int × Nat) : ¬ (better a b ∧ better b a) := by
  unfold better; omega

/-- …and transitive, so the reduction's result does not depend on the shuffle order. -/
theorem better_trans (a b c : Int × Nat) (h1 : better a b) (h2 : better b c) : better a c := by
  unfold better at *; omega

/-- ids and weights of token t, rank r land in [0, T·10). -/
theorem route_out_index (t r T : Nat) (ht : t < T) (hr : r < 10) : t * 10 + r < T * 10 := by omega

-- § Strata blob dequant addressing

def O_D_CODES : Nat := 1280 * 640
def O_GU_SC : Nat := O_D_CODES + 2560 * 160
def O_D_SC : Nat := O_GU_SC + 1280 * 40 * 2

/-- The device offsets equal the CPU blob layout's (819200, 1228800, 1331200) and end at BLOB. -/
theorem offsets_match_cpu :
    O_D_CODES = 819200 ∧ O_GU_SC = 1228800 ∧ O_D_SC = 1331200 ∧ O_D_SC + 2560 * 10 * 2 = 1382400 := by
  decide

/-- One thread per code byte: the launch size. -/
theorem dequant_threads : 1280 * 640 + 2560 * 160 = 1228800 := by decide

/-- Gate/up thread i: row < 1280, scale index inside the 1280·40 table, outputs inside 1280·2560. -/
theorem gu_thread_bounds (i k : Nat) (hi : i < 1280 * 640) (hk : k < 4) :
    i / 640 < 1280 ∧ (i / 640) * 40 + (i % 640) * 4 / 64 < 1280 * 40 ∧
      (i / 640) * 2560 + (i % 640) * 4 + k < 1280 * 2560 := by omega

/-!
# MODULE: prefill_chunk_pipeline
SOURCES: src/prefill/prefill.cpp
The host side of chunked prefill: the bump allocator (`Alloc::take`) and the claim that `bytes_needed`
sizes a borrowed region exactly; the chunk loop over the prompt; the PLE previous-token window; the
counting-sort grouping of (token, k) pairs by expert; and the 8-slot host→device staging ring whose
lookahead of STAGE−1 never reuses a slot still in flight.

## Source semantics
* `take(n)` reserves `((n·sizeof(T) + 256 + 255) & ~255)` bytes: a 256-aligned size with ≥ 256 bytes of
  slack.  From a region it fails iff `used + bytes > cap`; count-only mode only sums.
* `bytes_needed` replays `init`'s take sequence in count-only mode, so `init` from a region of that size
  never fails.
* Chunks: c0 = 0, T, 2T, …; size min(T, n − c0); they cover the prompt.
* `prev` after the chunk loop holds the last two tokens.
* Grouping: cnt[e] = #pairs routed to e, off = exclusive prefix sum; off[NE] = T·K when all ids < NE.
* Staging slot of the j-th streamed expert is j mod 8; with lookahead 7, two experts in flight together
  always use different slots.

## Form template identifiers
alignTake → takeBytes, runAlloc → bumpAllocate, total → countOnlyBytes, chunkSizes → promptChunks,
shiftPrev → pleWindow, offOf → expertOffset, stageSlot → stagingSlot
-/

namespace Strata.Prefill.Pipeline

-- § the bump allocator

/-- Bytes reserved for a raw request of x bytes: `(x + 511) & ~255`. -/
def alignTake (x : Nat) : Nat := (x + 511) / 256 * 256

/-- Every reservation is 256-byte aligned, so every bump pointer stays aligned. -/
theorem alignTake_aligned (x : Nat) : alignTake x % 256 = 0 := by
  unfold alignTake; omega

/-- A reservation always covers the request plus at least 256 bytes of slack. -/
theorem alignTake_covers (x : Nat) : x + 256 ≤ alignTake x ∧ alignTake x ≤ x + 511 := by
  unfold alignTake; omega

/-- `x & ~255` on the byte count is rounding down to a multiple of 256. -/
theorem mask_example : (1000 + 511) / 256 * 256 = 1280 := by decide

/-- Sequential takes from a region of capacity `cap`; `none` is the first failure. -/
def runAlloc (cap : Nat) : Nat → List Nat → Option Nat
  | used, [] => some used
  | used, x :: t => if used + alignTake x > cap then none else runAlloc cap (used + alignTake x) t

/-- Count-only mode: the sum of all reservations. -/
def total : List Nat → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | x :: t => alignTake x + total t

/-- A successful allocation used exactly the count-only total and stayed within capacity. -/
theorem runAlloc_some (cap used : Nat) (xs : List Nat) (u : Nat) (h : runAlloc cap used xs = some u) :
    u = used + total xs ∧ u ≤ cap ∨ (xs = [] ∧ u = used) := by
  induction xs generalizing used with
  | nil =>
    simp only [runAlloc, Option.some.injEq] at h
    right; exact ⟨rfl, h.symm⟩
  | cons x t ih =>
    simp only [runAlloc] at h
    split at h
    · contradiction
    · rename_i hc
      left
      rcases ih _ h with ⟨h1, h2⟩ | ⟨h1, h2⟩
      · simp only [total]; omega
      · subst h1; simp only [total]; omega

/-- `bytes_needed` is sufficient: from a region at least the counted size, `init` never fails. -/
theorem runAlloc_fits (cap used : Nat) (xs : List Nat) (h : used + total xs ≤ cap) :
    runAlloc cap used xs = some (used + total xs) := by
  induction xs generalizing used with
  | nil => simp [runAlloc, total]
  | cons x t ih =>
    simp only [runAlloc, total] at h ⊢
    have hnot : ¬ (used + alignTake x > cap) := by omega
    rw [if_neg hnot, ih (used + alignTake x) (by omega)]
    congr 1; omega

/-- The exact statement of `bytes_needed`: the counted size (slack aside) is enough for `init`. -/
theorem bytes_needed_exact (xs : List Nat) (slack : Nat) :
    runAlloc (total xs + slack) 0 xs = some (total xs) := by
  have := runAlloc_fits (total xs + slack) 0 xs (by omega)
  simpa using this

-- § chunking the prompt

/-- Chunk sizes min(T, n − c0) of the loop `for (c0 = 0; c0 < n; c0 += T)`. -/
def chunkSizes (T : Nat) (hT : 0 < T) : Nat → List Nat
  | n => if h : n = 0 then [] else min T n :: chunkSizes T hT (n - min T n)
termination_by n => n
decreasing_by omega

/-- The chunks cover the whole prompt. -/
theorem chunkSizes_sum (T : Nat) (hT : 0 < T) (n : Nat) : (chunkSizes T hT n).foldr (· + ·) 0 = n := by
  induction n using Nat.strongRecOn with
  | ind n ih =>
    rw [chunkSizes]
    split
    · simp_all
    · simp only [List.foldr_cons]
      rw [ih (n - min T n) (by omega)]
      omega

/-- Every chunk is non-empty and at most T tokens (fits the chunk buffers). -/
theorem chunkSizes_bounds (T : Nat) (hT : 0 < T) (n c : Nat) (hc : c ∈ chunkSizes T hT n) :
    0 < c ∧ c ≤ T := by
  induction n using Nat.strongRecOn with
  | ind n ih =>
    rw [chunkSizes] at hc
    split at hc
    · simp at hc
    · rename_i h
      rcases List.mem_cons.mp hc with h' | h'
      · omega
      · exact ih (n - min T n) (by omega) h'

-- § the PLE previous-token window

/-- `prev[0] = prev[1]; prev[1] = tok`. -/
def shiftPrev (p : Int × Int) (tok : Int) : Int × Int := (p.2, tok)

/-- After any prompt ending in a, b the window holds (a, b), whatever came before. -/
theorem window_last_two (p : Int × Int) (xs : List Int) (a b : Int) :
    (xs ++ [a, b]).foldl shiftPrev p = (a, b) := by
  rw [List.foldl_append]
  rfl

-- § grouping (token, k) pairs by expert

/-- `off[e]`: number of routed ids below e (exclusive prefix of the counts). -/
def offOf (ids : List Nat) (e : Nat) : Nat := (ids.filter (fun i => decide (i < e))).length

/-- `off[e+1] = off[e] + cnt[e]`. -/
theorem off_succ (ids : List Nat) (e : Nat) : offOf ids (e + 1) = offOf ids e + ids.count e := by
  induction ids with
  | nil => simp [offOf]
  | cons a t ih =>
    simp only [offOf, List.filter_cons, List.count_cons] at ih ⊢
    by_cases h1 : a < e
    · have h2 : a < e + 1 := by omega
      have h3 : ¬ (a == e) = true := by simp; omega
      simp [h1, h2, h3, ih]; omega
    · by_cases h4 : a = e
      · subst h4
        simp [ih]
      · have h2 : ¬ a < e + 1 := by omega
        have h3 : ¬ (a == e) = true := by simp; omega
        simp [h1, h2, h3, ih]

/-- `off[0] = 0`. -/
theorem off_zero (ids : List Nat) : offOf ids 0 = 0 := by simp [offOf]

/-- With every id in range, `off[NE]` is the number of pairs: every slot of the gathered buffer is used. -/
theorem off_last (ids : List Nat) (NE : Nat) (h : ∀ i ∈ ids, i < NE) : offOf ids NE = ids.length := by
  unfold offOf
  rw [List.filter_eq_self.mpr (by intro i hi; simpa using h i hi)]

/-- Expert ranges are ordered: off is monotone in e. -/
theorem off_mono (ids : List Nat) (e : Nat) : offOf ids e ≤ offOf ids (e + 1) := by
  rw [off_succ]; omega

-- § the staging ring

def STAGE : Nat := 8

/-- Slot of the j-th streamed expert. -/
def stageSlot (j : Nat) : Nat := j % STAGE

/-- Two experts in flight together (at most STAGE−1 = lookahead apart) use different slots. -/
theorem stage_slots_distinct (a b : Nat) (hab : a < b) (hclose : b ≤ a + (STAGE - 1)) :
    stageSlot a ≠ stageSlot b := by
  simp only [stageSlot, STAGE] at *
  omega

/-- The dequantized ring alternates: consecutive experts use different FP16 buffers. -/
theorem dq_alternates (j : Nat) : j % 2 ≠ (j + 1) % 2 := by omega

end Strata.Prefill.Pipeline

/-- Chunk sizes min(T, n − c0) of the loop `for (c0 = 0; c0 < n; c0 += T)`. -/
def chunkSizes (T : Nat) (hT : 0 < T) : Nat → List Nat

termination_by n => n
decreasing_by omega

/-- The chunks cover the whole prompt. -/
theorem chunkSizes_sum (T : Nat) (hT : 0 < T) (n : Nat) : (chunkSizes T hT n).foldr (· + ·) 0 = n := by
  induction n using Nat.strongRecOn with
  | ind n ih =>
    rw [chunkSizes]
    split
    · simp_all
    · simp only [List.foldr_cons]
      rw [ih (n - min T n) (by omega)]
      omega

/-- Every chunk is non-empty and at most T tokens (fits the chunk buffers). -/
theorem chunkSizes_bounds (T : Nat) (hT : 0 < T) (n c : Nat) (hc : c ∈ chunkSizes T hT n) :
    0 < c ∧ c ≤ T := by
  induction n using Nat.strongRecOn with
  | ind n ih =>
    rw [chunkSizes] at hc
    split at hc
    · simp at hc

def shiftPrev (p : Int × Int) (tok : Int) : Int × Int := (p.2, tok)

theorem window_last_two (p : Int × Int) (xs : List Int) (a b : Int) :
    (xs ++ [a, b]).foldl shiftPrev p = (a, b) := by
  rw [List.foldl_append]

/-- `off[e]`: number of routed ids below e (exclusive prefix of the counts). -/
def offOf (ids : List Nat) (e : Nat) : Nat := (ids.filter (fun i => decide (i < e))).length

/-- `off[e+1] = off[e] + cnt[e]`. -/
theorem off_succ (ids : List Nat) (e : Nat) : offOf ids (e + 1) = offOf ids e + ids.count e := by
  induction ids with
  | nil => simp [offOf]
  | cons a t ih =>

| Module | Sources | What's proved |
|---|---|---|
| **Q2RowDotIdentity** | expert.cpp, q2_avx2.cpp, expert.hpp | • 2-bit packing round-trips. • `Σ(c−1)x = Σcx − Σx`. • A row's accumulator minus its `hx` correction equals the exact value, with each 64-weight block using its own two chunk scales. • The oracle reduction gives the same value. • Using one scale per block is a real error (counterexample). • Multi-token results equal the single-token result for each token. |
| **Q2ExpertBlobGeometry** | expert.hpp, expert.cpp, expert_layout.cpp | • BLOB = 1,382,400 and the four regions fill it exactly. • Every row, scale and code-byte address stays inside its region. • The CPUID feature check (`usable`) and the OS check (XCR0 0xE6). |
| **ActivationQuantQ8** | expert.cpp, q2_avx2.cpp | • Legacy rounding (half away from zero) and the oracle's (half to even) differ exactly on odd ties, such as 1/2. • Clamp range and idempotence. • A zero chunk quantizes to all zeros. • A 32-element chunk's sum stays within ±4064, so int32 can't overflow. • Processing in vector lanes gives the same result as the scalar loop. |

| **ExpertPoolScheduling** | pool.cpp | • The `head_` counter runs every job exactly once. • Task row ranges add up to all rows. • Ranges that span two experts always make progress. • `parts` gives at least 3 tasks per thread. • Expert batching covers every expert. • The park counter returns to `n`. |
| **IQuantBlockDecode** | iq_avx512.cpp (+ native/avx2 dispatch) | • The 5 supported formats and their byte sizes. • Every byte each decoder reads stays inside its block. • Scales are odd, from 1 to 31. • How the sign mask flips the product. • Token groups of at most 4 cover every token. |
| **PrefillDeviceKernels** | kernels.cu | • `blocks_for` launches enough threads. • `gr_write` index decoding. • The router's lane/slot split, and its tie-break is a strict total order, so all lanes agree on the winner. • The GPU dequantizer's offsets match the CPU blob layout. • KV-append rows can't collide. |
| **PrefillChunkPipeline** | prefill.cpp | • The aligned bump allocator: `bytes_needed` is always enough for `init`. • Prompt chunks cover the whole prompt. • The PLE window keeps the last two tokens. • The expert offset table satisfies `off[e+1] = off[e] + cnt[e]` and ends at T·K. • Experts in flight at the same time never share a staging slot. |
